findings.evidence: maintenance documentation will be supplied and the operating system will be tested
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits which party (Yoggie Corporation or the Web Store developers) is responsible for supplying maintenance documentation and testing the operating system.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: Duplicates the requirement in GJ-003 that the system shall use a SQL-based database.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: Omits the grammatical subject/actor specifying what system or component must use a SQL-based database.

findings.evidence: Compatibility is only tested and verified for Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6 and 7, Netscape Communicator Version 4 and 5.
findings.rationale: Duplicates the exact list of supported browsers and versions already mandated in GJ-001.

findings.evidence: Other versions may not be 100% compatible. Also other browsers such as Mozilla or Firefox may not be 100% compatible.
findings.rationale: Uses non-committal weak phrasing ('may not be 100% compatible') and open-ended enumeration ('such as') without defining required behavior for unsupported browsers or versions.

findings.evidence: Shall install online help for users via the web interface
findings.rationale: Omits the responsible subject/actor who shall install the online help (e.g., developers, administrator, or installer).

findings.evidence: Shall deliver Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: Omits the responsible actor who shall deliver the specified documentation.

findings.evidence: Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: Modifier attachment ambiguity: it is unclear whether 'for the Administrator' applies only to 'Installation Instructions' or to all three listed documents.

findings.evidence: Assume the delivery of development, test and evaluate samples of the USB system from Yoggie.
findings.rationale: Does not specify the quantity of samples required, the delivery schedule/deadline, or the receiving party.

findings.evidence: after delivery
findings.rationale: 'after delivery' has an unclear referent: it does not specify whether the baseline is frozen after delivery of the samples in GJ-009 or after delivery of the final production USB system.

findings.evidence: Assume Yoggie will freeze the baseline of the USB system after delivery.
findings.rationale: Omits the duration of the baseline freeze, the exact delivery milestone that triggers it, and any exception or change-control conditions.

findings.evidence: shall be able to be deployed and operational
findings.rationale: Uses the weak capability phrase 'shall be able to' in passive voice and leaves 'deployed and operational' undefined (e.g., OS booted vs. web store accepting transactions).

findings.evidence: handle 1000 customers logged in concurrently
findings.rationale: 'handle' is vague and unmeasurable without defining acceptable response times, error rates, or functional expectations under the 1000-concurrent-customer load.

findings.evidence: email customer and vendor in less than 1 second
findings.rationale: Unclear whether the 1-second limit applies to emailing both customer and vendor combined or each individually, and whether 'email' refers to server dispatch or inbox delivery.

findings.evidence: The system shall be able to email customer and vendor in less than 1 second.
findings.rationale: Does not specify the triggering event or condition under which the system emails the customer and vendor (e.g., order placement or cancellation).

findings.evidence: will do periodic backups
findings.rationale: 'periodic' is vague and subjective, and 'will' weakens the requirement compared to 'shall'.

findings.evidence: periodic backups through a live internet connection
findings.rationale: Omits the concrete backup interval/frequency, backup scope and destination, and error handling when the live internet connection is unavailable.

findings.evidence: validate credit cards against fraud
findings.rationale: Does not define the fraud-detection criteria, checks, or external verification service/standard required to validate credit cards against fraud.

findings.evidence: The system shall validate credit cards against fraud.
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system shall respond when a credit card fails fraud validation or fraud is detected.

findings.evidence: all sensitive information
findings.rationale: 'sensitive information' is undefined; the requirement does not specify which data elements (e.g., passwords, payment details, personal info) qualify as sensitive.

findings.evidence: encrypt all customer data in database
findings.rationale: Does not specify the required encryption algorithm, standard, or minimum key length.

findings.evidence: auto detect IP DOS attacks and block IP automatically
findings.rationale: Omits the detection thresholds/criteria defining an IP DOS attack, the duration of the IP block, and any unblocking or false-positive handling conditions.

findings.evidence: The system shall detect consecutive failed login attempts.
findings.rationale: Specifies only detection with no resulting system action/consequence (e.g., account lockout or alert), and omits the threshold count of consecutive failed attempts and time window.

findings.evidence: availability of 99.99%
findings.rationale: Omits the measurement period (e.g., monthly or annually) and whether scheduled maintenance or patching windows are excluded from availability calculations.

findings.evidence: perform searches via Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm
findings.rationale: 'perform searches' is vague: it does not identify which searches are covered or define the graph nodes and edge weights required to apply Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm.

findings.evidence: validate 'existing' credit card in system
findings.rationale: 'existing' (even placed in quotes) is ambiguous regarding which stored card(s) are checked (e.g., default vs. all saved cards) and what validation checks are performed.

findings.evidence: validate 'existing' credit card in system after each log in
findings.rationale: Does not specify what the system shall do if an existing credit card fails validation upon login.

findings.evidence: too large in size
findings.rationale: 'too large in size' is subjective and unmeasurable without an explicit threshold.

findings.evidence: automatically compress image files that are too large in size
findings.rationale: Omits the maximum file-size threshold (with units, e.g., KB/MB) that triggers compression as well as the target compressed size, format, or quality level.

findings.evidence: will employ on demand asynchronous loading for faster execution of pages
findings.rationale: 'faster execution' is a vague, unmeasurable comparative with no baseline or numeric target, and 'will' is weaker than 'shall'.

findings.evidence: validate email address existence
findings.rationale: Does not clarify how existence is validated (e.g., syntax/MX record lookup, SMTP check, or confirmation email verification).

findings.evidence: The system shall validate email address existence.
findings.rationale: Does not specify what the system shall do when an email address does not exist or cannot be verified, nor which events trigger validation.

findings.evidence: easy to use
findings.rationale: 'easy to use' is subjective and unverifiable without measurable usability criteria.

findings.evidence: easy to learn
findings.rationale: 'easy to learn' is subjective and unverifiable without measurable learnability metrics such as maximum training time or first-use task completion rate.

findings.evidence: utilize help bubbles to assist managers, customers, and administrators
findings.rationale: Does not specify which UI elements or workflows include help bubbles, how they are triggered or dismissed, or what content they must provide.

findings.evidence: easy to locate buttons
findings.rationale: 'easy to locate' is subjective and unverifiable without specific UI layout, placement, or visual-contrast criteria.

findings.evidence: friend easy to read error messages
findings.rationale: 'friend easy to read' (typo for 'friendly, easy to read') is subjective and unverifiable without concrete tone, readability, or message-content criteria.

findings.evidence: consistent symbols and colors for clear notifications
findings.rationale: 'consistent' and 'clear' are vague and unmeasurable without defining the specific symbol set, color scheme, or notification standards.

findings.evidence: interchangeable plugins
findings.rationale: 'interchangeable plugins' is vague because it does not define the supported plugin types, interfaces/APIs, or interoperability criteria.

findings.evidence: easily updatable
findings.rationale: 'easily updatable' is subjective and unverifiable without defining the update mechanism, allowable downtime, or measurable effort criteria.

findings.evidence: easy to upgrade
findings.rationale: 'easy to upgrade' is subjective and unverifiable without measurable upgrade criteria, procedures, or downtime limits.

findings.evidence: extremely portable
findings.rationale: 'extremely portable' is subjective and unverifiable without concrete portability metrics, supported host environments, or setup requirements.

findings.evidence: the usb drive
findings.rationale: Refers to the hardware platform inconsistently as 'the usb drive' instead of 'the USB system' used in GJ-009 and GJ-010.

findings.evidence: easy to migrate or backed up via another usb drive
findings.rationale: 'easy to migrate' is subjective and unmeasurable, and it is unclear whether 'another usb drive' refers to a standard storage drive or another Yoggie USB system.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding modal 'should' combined with the weak capability phrase 'be able to', leaving it ambiguous whether debug mode is mandatory.

findings.evidence: run under debug mode
findings.rationale: Does not specify what capabilities or outputs debug mode provides, how it is activated/deactivated, or who is authorized to enable it.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding modal 'should' combined with the weak capability phrase 'be able to', making requirement obligation unclear.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding modal 'should' combined with the weak capability phrase 'be able to', making requirement obligation unclear.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding modal 'should' combined with the weak capability phrase 'be able to', making requirement obligation unclear.

findings.evidence: weborder system
findings.rationale: Refers to the product as 'weborder system' instead of 'Web Store' used consistently in GJ-001, GJ-002, and GJ-005.

findings.evidence: system hardware shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection
findings.rationale: Physical hardware cannot be patched over an internet connection, leaving it ambiguous whether firmware, operating system, or software patching is intended.

findings.evidence: shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits which party (Yoggie Corporation, developers, or administrator) is responsible for providing and applying the fixes and patches.

findings.evidence: The system hardware shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection.
findings.rationale: Conflicts with GJ-010's assumption that Yoggie will freeze the baseline of the USB system after delivery.

findings.evidence: our organization
findings.rationale: 'our organization' has no defined referent in the document, and 'coordinate on future enhancement and features' is vague and unverifiable.

findings.evidence: OS: Apache web server
findings.rationale: Lists 'OS: Apache web server' (and includes OS and Database under 'hardware requirements'), contradicting GJ-002 which specifies Slackware Linux 2.6 as the operating system and Apache Web Server as the web server.
